A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same L4Q research work, despite the revised title and organization. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v3 includes readable Appendices A-C.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-cost measurements, Commonsense QA and MMLU evaluations, and quantization-parameter ablations in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and memory results, QAT-LoRA comparisons in Figure 3, and warm-up experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Core L4Q retains merge-before-quantization and joint LoRA, scale and bias training. Scale initialization changes from AbsMax/2^(n-1) in v1 Equation 6 to AbsMax/Qp, with Qp=2^(n-1)-1, in v3 Algorithm 1. v3 also introduces decoupled QAT-LoRA as an intermediate comparison variant. Its prose gives a conflicting Qp formula, leaving the implemented divisor unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions fine-tune on Stanford Alpaca and evaluate the same Commonsense QA suite and zero-/five-shot MMLU tasks. OpenLLaMA 3B adds a model configuration, while the warm-up study changes training procedures; neither introduces different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds QAT-LoRA as an accuracy comparator in Figure 3 and introduces QAT versus QAT-LoRA memory comparisons. QA-LoRA is added to the 13B/33B Commonsense QA comparisons and all MMLU model-size comparisons. GPTQ+LoRA corresponds to the renamed uniform-quantization QLoRA*: all shared rows retain identical scores, so this is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: v3 revises L4Q learning rates and changes learning-rate warm-up from 50 of 200 steps to 10% of training. QA-LoRA's stated batch size and quantization group size change from 16 and 32 to 128 and 128 for LLaMA. OpenLLaMA 3B configurations and a 100-step warm-up experiment are added. These reported setting changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's scale-initialization and scale-versus-bias ablations, including divergence observations, are removed rather than relocated. v3 adds a coupled L4Q versus decoupled QAT-LoRA analysis in Figure 3 and a sweep over 0, 10, 20, 40 and 80 warm-up steps for two 7B models in Appendix B. These test substantially different methodological questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Many LLaMA-1 results are replaced: Table 3's 7B 4-bit L4Q zero-/five-shot averages change from 33.5/32.4 to 34.9/35.7, while its 3-bit zero-shot average changes from 31.2 to 30.6. Changed reported settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. v3 adds comparator and warm-up results but removes the earlier L4Q training-cost and initialization-ablation entries; shared QLoRA* and LLaMA-2 Commonsense QA results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds chain-rule and STE derivations supporting the existing quantization and LoRA updates, including clipping cases and activation-based gradient expressions. v3 Equation 7 restores the alpha factors missing from v1 Equations 8-9. These are formal additions and corrections to the existing gradient mathematics.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes applicability to full-precision or pre-quantized models, half-precision training efficiency and performance comparable to QA-LoRA. v3 centers its contributions on coupled adaptation outperforming constrained QA-LoRA and decoupled QAT-LoRA, introducing the latter explicitly. The earlier highlighted claims about comparable training time and single-GPU 33B memory feasibility are no longer presented as contributions.

C2.justification: v3 develops a coupling-based explanation of accuracy and interprets prolonged warm-up as leaving insufficient quantization-recovery training. Its new limitations section explicitly identifies weight-only scope and unmeasured inference speed requiring custom kernels. v1 instead emphasizes initialization/outlier preservation, optimizer precision and the unresolved memory cost of storing unquantized weights; those discussions are substantially reduced or removed.

D1.justification: Technical reporting changes substantially. v3 newly specifies the 50k/2k Alpaca split, QA-LoRA rank 8, baseline-specific learning rates and maximum sequence length 1304. These disclosures do not establish changes from previously unstated settings. Conversely, v1's explicit bfloat16-versus-FP32 optimizer-state information, memory-measurement procedure and LoRA reference-model training budget are omitted.

R1.justification: The central LoRA/LSQ and quantization-aware PEFT literature remains. v3 sharpens criticism of QA-LoRA's constrained adaptation, adds supporting works including STE, PACT, Optimal Brain Compression and KVQuant, and removes AlphaTuning and OWQ. Numerous other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The title, acronym expansion, abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work and technical background are reorganized into Section 2, the method narrative now progresses through QAT-LoRA to L4Q, and separate limitations and appendix sections replace much of the earlier organization.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 becomes an accuracy/model-size diagram, Figure 2 is redrawn around four training/inference schemes, and Figure 3 adds comparative bar charts. The resource table is replaced, benchmark tables expand, and new warm-up and hyperparameter tables appear in the appendices.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens support for the central coupling argument through the direct QAT-LoRA comparison and broader QA-LoRA evaluations, while adding gradient derivations and clearer inference-speed limitations. These gains are offset by removing v1's direct L4Q training-cost measurements, initialization ablations and optimizer-precision details. Accuracy interpretations also remain overbroad: v3 Table 3 reports 13B 4-bit five-shot MMLU accuracy of 46.0 for L4Q versus 46.9 for QLoRA*, despite the stated general superiority.
